originalTitle: How Much Could You Lose In Plug Power Stock?
summary: Shares of Plug Power (PLUG) dropped 20% over the past month. The company reported no financial results during that time, and the broader market actually gained ground, with the S&P 500 rising 1.8%. For anyone holding the shares, that disconnect raises an obvious concern regarding what happens when the whole market turns down. Since 2007, the company has traded through 15 market shocks. So how much has Plug Power lost when the market itself fell.
content:
Shares of Plug Power (PLUG) dropped 20% over the past month. The company reported no financial results during that time, and the broader market actually gained ground, with the S&P 500 rising 1.8%. For anyone holding the shares, that disconnect raises an obvious concern regarding what happens when the whole market turns down. Since 2007, the company has traded through 15 market shocks . So how much has Plug Power lost when the market itself fell?

Plug Holders Gave Up Nearly Half On Average

Plug’s deepest loss during those shocks was 84% in the 2008-2009 Global Financial Crisis, a period when the S&P 500 lost 53%. That 84% decline was not a broader market fall alone: it includes a one-day break in the stock price on September 29, 2008. A similar pattern emerged when oil prices fell from 2014 to 2016. In that window, Plug lost 73% while the S&P 500 lost 6.8%. Across all the shocks, the stock fell 47.7% on average, against a 15.8% decline for the index.

Rebound times have varied wildly for investors trying to break even. Following 12 of the historical shocks, Plug eventually returned to its pre-shock high, with a median wait of 5.5 months from the lowest point. Yet five of those recoveries took more than a year, and the rebound following the 2008-2009 crisis took 142 months. Furthermore, the stock has still not recovered from three specific shocks. Most notably, the shares remain 95% below the high they reached before the 2022 inflation shock.

The company sells hydrogen equipment, such as electrolyzers and fuel cell systems, but has yet to turn a profit. The financial bleeding, however, is slowing down. In the second quarter of 2026, Plug recorded a gross loss of about 0.9% of revenue. That is a sharp improvement from the 30.7% gross loss it reported a year earlier. Over the last twelve months, the operating loss equaled 68% of revenue, down from 135% the year before. While these negative margins are shrinking, the core reality remains that Plug spends more than it brings in.

At the same time, top-line momentum is cooling. Revenue rose just 2.5% from a year earlier in the latest quarter, following a 22% increase in the prior period. Investors are also facing significant dilution. Plug’s share count rose 132.6% in three years, meaning each share represents a smaller fraction of the overall business. The company also carries a heavier debt load relative to its size than the S&P 500. Its debt equals 44.1% of its market value, against 20.6% for the index.

Management Is Counting On A Big Fourth Quarter

Plug expects most of its financial progress for 2026 to materialize in the final months of the year. During an August 10 call, management noted that second-half sales will be 40% higher than in the first half, mostly from equipment. The company anticipates that the majority of its second-half volume will arrive in the fourth quarter. Management also raised its full-year forecast for 2026 revenue growth to a range of 15% to 16%, up from 13% to 15%.

While waiting for that year-end activity, the company continues to burn through capital. Plug ended the second quarter with $161.9 million of cash it was free to spend, and its net cash use was $61 million during the period. The company aims to raise more than $275 million by selling assets and securing financing that issues no new shares. A potential wrinkle involves Texas, where the governor wants data center projects in the state reviewed. When asked on the August 10 call whether that would affect the sale of Plug’s assets there, management said it expects the review to run its course and confirmed it is still working on that sale.

Moving forward, management stated that Plug remains on track to achieve positive EBITDA, a measure of profit before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization, in the fourth quarter. If EBITDA is still below zero in that quarter, it would show that the company’s plan for the year is running behind.

Does This Mean You Should Act On PLUG?

Our purpose is to inform you with unique data so you make the right investment decisions. That said, betting on a single stock is always risky, no matter which direction you choose.

There is a smarter approach. Since its inception, the Trefis High Quality (HQ) Portfolio has returned 105%, beating the benchmark that combines the three major indices – the S&P 500, S&P Mid-cap, and Russell 2000.
